Minor Account
Under 18 · Guardian-Operated · Demat-Only · Offline
Offline (Kotak Branch)
Kotak Securities supports demat accounts for minors (below 18) operated by a natural guardian. The account is strictly demat-only — no live trading until the minor turns 18. Process via Kotak branch with guardian's KYC, minor's birth certificate and PAN.

Joint Demat Account
Two or More Holders · Not Available
Kotak Securities does not support joint demat or joint trading accounts. SEBI regulations permit joint demat accounts at depositories, but Kotak Securities' account structure does not offer this option. Each investor must hold a separate individual demat account. If you specifically require a joint demat account, consider ICICI Securities or full-service brokers that offer this facility via NSDL/CDSL.

Foreign National / OCI (Non-Kotak Bank)
OCI / PIO without Kotak Bank Account · Not Available
Foreign nationals, OCI holders, and PIOs who do not already bank with Kotak Mahindra Bank cannot open a Kotak Securities account directly. Kotak Securities' NRI account onboarding is tightly integrated with Kotak Bank's NRI banking — applicants must first open a Kotak Bank NRE/NRO account before being eligible. Non-Kotak-banking NRIs should consider ICICI Securities or other brokers with broader NRI onboarding pathways.

Advantages & Disadvantages

Pros & Cons

An honest assessment of where Kotak Securities excels and where it falls short compared to discount brokers in 2026.

✅
Advantages
  • ✓3-in-1 Account with Kotak Bank: Seamless integration with Kotak Bank savings, demat, and trading — instant fund transfers 24/7, no NEFT/UPI lag, auto-payout back to savings at night.
  • ✓Trade Free Plan — Zero Delivery Brokerage: The Trade Free plan offers ₹0 delivery brokerage and ₹20 flat F&O — genuinely competitive with Zerodha. Kotak Securities delivers discount pricing with full-service reliability.
  • ✓In-House Research: SEBI-registered equity research covering 300+ stocks with daily reports, model portfolios, and sector analysis — unavailable at discount brokers.
  • ✓Bank-Backed Safety: 100% subsidiary of Kotak Mahindra Bank — India's 4th largest private bank with institutional credibility and a 30-year track record in broking.
  • ✓Trade Free Youth Plan: Exclusive zero-cost plan for investors below 30 — zero delivery brokerage AND zero Demat AMC for the first year. Exceptional value for first-time investors.
  • ✓1,400+ Branches Pan-India: For investors who need in-person support, Kotak Securities has an extensive branch network backed by Kotak Mahindra Bank's infrastructure.
  • ✓Complete Kotak Group Ecosystem: Equities, MF (Kotak AMC), Life Insurance (Kotak Life), FD, and banking — all under one Kotak Securities login.
⚠️
Limitations
  • ✗Classic Plan Still Expensive: The Classic Plan charges 0.49% on delivery trades — similar to HDFC Securities' classic plan. New users who don't switch to Trade Free are inadvertently paying premium brokerage rates.
  • ✗No Joint Demat Accounts: Kotak Securities does not support joint demat or trading accounts — each investor must hold a separate individual account. ICICI Securities is a better option for couples/joint investors.
  • ✗NRI Onboarding Requires Kotak Bank Account: NRIs without an existing Kotak Mahindra Bank NRE/NRO account cannot directly open a Kotak Securities account. This is a prerequisite that competing brokers (ICICI Direct) don't require.
  • ✗Customer Service Quality: Customer service response times during volatile markets have been slower than expected for a bank-backed broker. Phone support wait times can extend to 30+ minutes during peak market hours.
  • ✗No NPS on Platform: National Pension Scheme is not available directly via the Kotak Securities platform — users need a separate NPS account from NPS Trust or another registered entity.
  • ✗App Stability Issues: Kotak Neo app has experienced intermittent crashes and login failures during high-volatility market events — a concern for active traders who cannot afford platform downtime.

What are Kotak Securities' brokerage charges in 2026?+
Kotak Securities offers three distinct brokerage plans. The Trade Free Plan is the most popular — ₹0 on delivery and ₹20 flat on all other segments. Below is a quick breakdown:

  • ✓Trade Free Plan: ₹0 equity delivery + ₹20 flat for intraday, futures, and options. Subscription ₹99/month or ₹999/year. Best plan for most users.
  • ✓Trade Free Youth Plan: Same as Trade Free — ₹0 delivery + ₹20 flat — but for investors below 30 years. Zero Demat AMC in first year. Subscription only ₹49/month after year 1.

How to open a Kotak Securities demat account?+
Opening a Kotak Securities demat account is fully online, paperless, and takes under 15 minutes for Kotak Bank customers. Non-Kotak Bank users can also apply online but may need to complete additional steps.
  • ✓Step 1 — Visit website or app: Go to kotaksecurities.com or download the Kotak Neo app. Click 'Open Demat Account'.
  • ✓Step 2 — Enter mobile number and PAN: OTP verification on your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. PAN validation against Income Tax records.
  • ✓Step 3 — Complete eKYC via DigiLocker: Aadhaar OTP-based KYC. Bank account verification via penny drop. Upload signature and selfie photo.
  • ✓Step 4 — e-Sign and submit: Digitally sign the account opening form via Aadhaar OTP e-sign. Account activation in 24–48 hours.
  • ★Documents needed: PAN card, Aadhaar (linked to mobile), bank account details (savings), and a signature image for digitisation.
✓ ₹0 for Kotak Bank Customers ₹750 for Non-Kotak Users 15 Minutes Process Fully Online & Paperless
💡 Kotak Bank customers get a zero-cost 3-in-1 account (bank + demat + trading). For non-Kotak Bank users, a ₹750 one-time account opening fee applies.

How does Kotak Securities compare to Zerodha in 2026?+
Kotak Securities and Zerodha are both strong choices in 2026, but they serve different investor profiles. Kotak excels in bank integration, research, and full-service support — Zerodha leads in platform speed, user experience, and algo trading tools.
  • ✓Kotak Trade Free vs Zerodha — brokerage is equal: Both charge ₹0 delivery and ₹20 flat F&O. Kotak Trade Free requires ₹99/month subscription, while Zerodha has no subscription fee.
  • ✓Kotak advantage — bank integration: 3-in-1 account with Kotak Bank provides instant fund transfers, auto-payout, and a single app for all banking + trading needs. Zerodha requires UPI/NEFT for fund transfers.
  • ★Kotak advantage — in-house research: SEBI-registered equity research, model portfolios, and advisory are available at Kotak. Zerodha has no in-house research — traders must use third-party tools.
  • !Zerodha advantage — Kite platform: Zerodha's Kite is widely regarded as India's best trading platform for speed, reliability, and UX. Kotak Neo is good but not at Kite's level.
  • !Zerodha advantage — algo trading: Zerodha Streak for no-code algo trading is unmatched. Kotak has no native algo builder.
Best Choice By Profile
  • ✓Choose Kotak if: You bank with Kotak Mahindra Bank, value research and advisory, need NRI/corporate accounts, or want an integrated bank-broker ecosystem.
  • ★Choose Zerodha if: You are a pure active trader, prioritise platform UX, need algo trading (Streak), or don't want a monthly subscription.
📊 Bottom line: Kotak Securities is the better choice for Kotak Bank customers and research-driven investors. Zerodha is better for pure traders who don't need bank integration.

What account types does Kotak Securities NOT support?+
Kotak Securities is comprehensive but has notable account type gaps compared to some full-service brokers like ICICI Securities — joint demat accounts, direct NRI onboarding for non-Kotak Bank customers, and standalone demat-only accounts are not available.
  • !Joint Demat Accounts: Kotak Securities does not offer joint demat or joint trading accounts. Each investor must hold a separate individual account. If you need a joint account, consider ICICI Securities, which supports joint demat accounts via CDSL.
  • !Foreign Nationals / OCI without Kotak Bank: OCI holders, PIOs, and foreign nationals who do not already bank with Kotak Mahindra Bank cannot directly apply for a Kotak Securities account. They must first open a Kotak Bank NRE/NRO account.
  • !Standalone Demat-Only Account: Kotak Securities requires all demat accounts to be bundled with a trading account. If you need pure demat holding (without active trading), this structure may not suit you.

  • ✓Corporate Accounts: Pvt Ltd, LLP, Partnership, Trust — dedicated RM assigned
  • ✓Minor Accounts: Under 18, guardian-operated, demat-only until majority
